subject.title: fix(line): dripping inbound media downloads hang past setup timeout

question: Should LINE inbound media bodies fail closed after a fixed 120-second wall-clock once HTTP 200 headers arrive?
rationale: The implementation safely enforces the limit, but choosing a fixed total lifetime intentionally trades indefinite-hang protection against delivery of legitimate transfers slower than the cutoff.

options.title: Confirm the 120-second cutoff
options.body: Accept the sibling-channel-aligned deadline because LINE downloads are already size-capped and the patch preserves a fresh transfer budget after readiness.

options.title: Use progress-aware expiry
options.body: Replace the fixed lifetime with a throughput or no-progress policy that still terminates pathological drips while permitting very slow continuously progressing transfers.

recommendation.title: Confirm the 120-second cutoff
recommendation.body: Accept the sibling-channel-aligned deadline because LINE downloads are already size-capped and the patch preserves a fresh transfer budget after readiness.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the current LINE readiness and stream-cancellation contract that this policy extends.
